summary: This code defines a RobotPet class that stores a name, a battery level, and a mood, plus a can_walk method that works out whether the battery can cover a walk of a given length. Two robot pets are then created so their walking ability can be tested.

lines.text: This begins the blueprint for a robot pet; every pet created from it will share the same structure and behaviour.
The __init__ method runs automatically whenever a new RobotPet is created, and it receives the three details that describe that pet.
The name passed in is stored on the object itself, so each pet remembers its own name after __init__ finishes.
The battery level is stored as an attribute because can_walk needs to read it later.
The mood is kept alongside the other details; it is not used by can_walk, but it is part of what describes a pet.
This method belongs to each pet, and self gives it access to that particular pet's battery when deciding about a walk of duration minutes.

lines.code: """Check if the pet has enough energy for a walk of given duration (in minutes)."""
lines.text: A docstring records what the method promises to do, which is exactly the behaviour an assert statement would later check.
The rule of this program is that every minute of walking costs two units of battery, so the cost is calculated before it is compared.
The comparison produces True or False, and returning it lets the caller decide what to do rather than printing a message here.
This creates a well-charged pet, a good case for checking that can_walk says yes.
Beep has less battery, so it is the case that shows can_walk correctly refusing a long walk.
